# RFC-0012: Repository-authoritative multi-agent coordination

> **Version:** 0.1.1 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** test
> **Owners:** @govctl-org

**References:** [RFC-0000](../rfc/RFC-0000.md), [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md), [RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md), [RFC-0006](../rfc/RFC-0006.md), [RFC-0010](../rfc/RFC-0010.md), [RFC-0011](../rfc/RFC-0011.md)

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0012:C-SCOPE] First-version scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0012c-scope"></a>

The first version coordinates repository-backed requests, exclusive ownership, explicit handoff and immutable outcome references. It publishes signed control records attached to RFCs, ADRs and Work Items. External clients authenticate participants, schedule or run agents, apply source or code changes, and invoke governed lifecycle operations. Completing a coordination request records its outcome; it is not evidence that code was merged, an artifact lifecycle advanced or a verification guard passed. Ordinary fast-forward publication to canonical main is supported; protected-branch automation, merge-queue integration, automatic takeover by elapsed time and a general agent runner are outside this version. Unsupported publication paths remain ineffective rather than emulating successful ownership.

*Since: v0.1.0*

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0012:C-AUTHORITY] Canonical repository authority (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-authority"></a>

In repository publication mode, the configured canonical repository's main branch MUST be the authority for shared request and execution-ownership state. An update MUST become effective only after successful publication on that branch and protocol validation against its actual predecessor. Unpublished local records and unmerged pull requests MUST NOT grant execution ownership. Invalid or unauthorized records MUST NOT confer execution rights. Independent clones observing the same accepted history and policy context MUST derive the same shared state.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-REQUEST] Attached requests and operation identity (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-request"></a>

A collaboration request MUST attach to an existing RFC, ADR or Work Item and identify its stable request identity, requested operation and exact input revision. That operation and input binding MUST be immutable; a different operation or input MUST require a new request identity. Claims MUST reference their request and its input binding. Completed or cancelled requests MUST NOT be claimed again or accept another completion. Requests, claims, handoffs and results MUST remain attached records rather than new governed task artifacts. Each state-changing operation MUST have a stable identity and semantic payload, including its actor, target and references to the state it changes. The same operation identity with different semantic content MUST be rejected; a retry with the same content MUST return the existing accepted result without duplicating its effects, including after request completion. A publication-parent witness MAY change during a retry without changing the operation's semantic intent.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-EXCLUSION] Exclusive modification and parallel review (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-exclusion"></a>

At most one current execution claim MUST authorize execution of a given request, including a read-only review request. A modifying request MUST additionally hold exclusive write claims for every existing artifact it changes; at most one current write claim MUST authorize modification of a given artifact. A modifying result MUST identify its full write scope, and its publication MUST be rejected unless its executing holder has the required current claims for that scope. New artifact identities MUST remain unique in accepted repository state. Distinct read-only review requests for the same immutable revision MAY run concurrently and MUST NOT acquire artifact write ownership merely by reviewing. A request that changes an artifact's lifecycle MUST satisfy the same write-ownership rules as a content modification, in addition to the existing lifecycle and verification requirements.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-PUBLICATION] Conditional publication and semantic revalidation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-publication"></a>

An accepted coordination update MUST advance canonical main by a conditional fast-forward against the exact authoritative parent used for its validation. Forced updates MUST NOT be accepted as protocol publication. A stale publication parent or conflicting claim MUST cause a conflict rather than silently granting authority. Granting execution authority or accepting an effective result against a changed input revision MUST cause a conflict. Changed input alone MUST NOT prevent cancellation, claim release or publication of explicitly ineffective history; those operations MUST still satisfy their applicable authorization and causal-state requirements. After a publication race, retrying clients MUST validate the operation against the newly observed authoritative state; a successful textual rebase alone MUST NOT establish semantic validity. When branch protection requires pull requests or a merge queue, the same conditions MUST hold at the final main update, and ownership MUST remain ineffective until that update succeeds.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-GENERATION] Claim generations and explicit transfer (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-generation"></a>

Accepted ownership transitions MUST use monotonically increasing generations for each request and each artifact write scope so that a previous holder cannot regain authority by replaying an old operation. A handoff offer MUST identify the current request and write-scope generations, intended recipient and checkpoint. Publishing an offer MUST NOT transfer execution authority; the offering holder retains it until an authorized transfer, release, cancellation or completion. Only the named recipient MAY accept a still-current offer. Acceptance MUST atomically transfer the request and its write scopes, advance their generations and invalidate the prior holder's authority. A takeover MUST name the affected scopes, their prior generations and the new holder, and MUST atomically invalidate the prior holder's authority over those scopes. The resulting claims MUST satisfy [RFC-0012:C-EXCLUSION](../rfc/RFC-0012.md#rfc-0012c-exclusion). Takeover MUST include an explicit authorization decision and reason. Release, cancellation and completion MUST invalidate the affected claims and outstanding offers for future effective results; an idempotent replay of an already accepted result remains valid under [RFC-0012:C-REQUEST](../rfc/RFC-0012.md#rfc-0012c-request). This version MUST NOT infer takeover or release solely from wall-clock age, a missing heartbeat or an unavailable process. Results from obsolete generations MUST NOT mutate artifacts or complete the current request.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-RESULT] Revision-bound results and code targets (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-result"></a>

Under the publication capability, a result MUST identify its request, actor, exact input revision, applicable request-claim generation and immutable outcome or resulting revision. An effective result MUST reference the current request-claim generation and, for a modifying result, all applicable current artifact write-claim generations at publication. A review MUST remain bound to the reviewed document digest and, for code review, an explicit immutable code commit; that code commit MUST NOT be inferred from the current coordination main HEAD. Coordination-only commits MUST NOT invalidate an approval whose document and code targets remain unchanged. Obsolete results MAY remain as explicitly ineffective history but MUST NOT be rebound to a newer input, claim or code revision. Accepted results MUST NOT bypass existing artifact lifecycle or guard requirements. These publication-mode bindings MUST NOT retroactively change the targets or interpretation of existing standalone collaboration records.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-POLICY] External authorization and explicit policy context (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-policy"></a>

Runtime scheduling, participant authentication, signer-to-subject bindings, permission management and credentials MUST remain responsibilities of external clients or authorities. govctl MUST validate protocol structure, revision bindings and causal state using explicit authorization and policy context supplied for the operation. Repository-embedded keys, actor roles or Git push permission alone MUST NOT establish execution or approval authority.

The external context MUST contain `protocolVersion: 1`, `repoId`, explicit `remote`, `branch: "main"`, `authorityId`, `currentPolicyRevision`, and a `policies` map keyed by policy revision. Remote MUST be an absolute filesystem path, HTTPS URL, SSH URL or SCP-style SSH repository address; local remote aliases, Git extension transports and command URLs MUST be rejected. The context and private signing key MUST NOT be published.

Each policy MUST contain `effectiveAfterCommit`, `trustedIssuers` and `grants`. A trusted issuer MUST identify its `keyId` and `publicKeyPem`; the key ID MUST be the SHA-256 of canonical LF Ed25519 SPKI PEM. A grant MUST bind `subjectId`, `issuerKeyId` and allowed `actions`. Policy activation anchors MUST be distinct commits on canonical main's first-parent chain. The latest activation at or before an operation's actual publication parent MUST determine the policy that authorizes it. Its signed authority and revision MUST match that policy. `currentPolicyRevision` MUST match the policy active at fetched main HEAD. Retained historical grants MUST NOT authorize a new event after a newer policy has become effective.

The authenticated actor and execution holder MUST remain separately attributable. A new holder MUST have a `claim` grant bound to the current signing issuer. An actor acting for a different holder MUST possess both the action grant and `delegate`, and MUST explicitly supply `onBehalfOf` equal to that holder's subject ID. A delegated action MUST NOT impersonate the holder in the event actor. Takeover MUST require its own action grant in addition to new-holder eligibility. Policy authority and revision MUST be recorded without credentials. Existing historical facts MAY remain verifiable after a policy change; replay MUST NOT turn them into a fresh authorization.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-COMPATIBILITY] Capability and existing-history compatibility (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-compatibility"></a>

Publication-mode clients MUST negotiate an explicit capability before relying on cross-clone execution ownership or publication-mode review targets. An unsupported capability MUST produce an unsupported-operation result rather than falling back to clone-local claims. Existing formatVersion 1 and 2 collaboration records MUST retain their bytes, identities and interpretation under [RFC-0011:C-COMPATIBILITY](../rfc/RFC-0011.md#rfc-0011c-compatibility); migration MUST NOT turn historical assignments or execution receipts into current ownership, or rebind historical reviews to publication-mode targets. The local claims, reservations and presence defined by [RFC-0010](../rfc/RFC-0010.md) MUST remain clone-local and MUST NOT be treated as distributed ownership witnesses. Existing standalone artifact commands and read-only views MUST remain usable without enabling repository publication mode.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-CLI] Coordination CLI and capability (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-cli"></a>

The first-version CLI MUST expose `govctl coord capabilities`, `govctl coord list --context-file PATH`, and `govctl coord apply --context-file PATH --sign-key-file PATH --stdin`. These commands MUST be independent of the caller's workspace and MUST NOT modify its source, index or branch. They MUST emit JSON on success. Failures MUST exit nonzero with a stable diagnostic marker on stderr.

Capabilities MUST report `protocolVersion: 1`, capability `repository-main-coordination-v1`, actions `publish`, `claim`, `handoff`, `accept`, `release`, `cancel`, `takeover`, `complete`, publication mode `direct-fast-forward`, and `sourceMutation: false`. Capabilities MUST work without a repository or context. Unsupported versions, actions or publication modes MUST fail closed. The first version MUST NOT apply source or code changes, invoke an agent runner, advance artifact lifecycles, or bypass branch protection. A rejected protected-main push MUST NOT be reported as a successful claim or as an automatically created pull request.

`list` MUST return `protocolVersion`, `repoId`, canonical `head`, `authority` with `id` and `revision`, `artifacts` containing canonical artifact `target` objects, `requests`, and `writes`. Each request MUST expose `requestId`, fixed `target`, `requestedOperation`, `description`, `writeTargets`, `status`, `stateEventId`, `generation`, nullable `holder`, nullable `handoff`, nullable `result`, and `stale`. Status MUST be `open`, `claimed`, `handoff`, `completed` or `cancelled`. Each write entry MUST retain `artifactId`, `generation`, nullable `requestId` and nullable `holder`, including generation tombstones after release. Stale source MUST NOT erase a request or its ownership history.

An apply receipt MUST contain `protocolVersion`, `operationId`, `requestId`, `eventId`, `publicationCommit`, observed `head`, `replayed`, `effective`, and the current projected `request`. Exact replay MUST return the original operation's effect classification with the current request projection. `--dry-run` MUST validate without publication and return `effective: false` and `publicationCommit: null`. Ineffective historical evidence MUST return `effective: false`. A receipt MUST NOT imply that an external runtime started.

The stable error markers MUST include `COORD_INVALID_INPUT`, `COORD_INVALID_CONTEXT`, `COORD_UNAUTHORIZED`, `COORD_POLICY_INVALID`, `COORD_HISTORY_INVALID`, `COORD_NOT_FOUND`, `COORD_SOURCE_CHANGED`, `COORD_STATE_CONFLICT`, `COORD_WRITE_CONFLICT`, `COORD_TERMINAL`, `COORD_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`, `COORD_PUBLISH_REJECTED`, `COORD_PUBLICATION_UNKNOWN`, `COORD_GIT_FAILED`, and `COORD_UNSUPPORTED`.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-PROTOCOL] First-version operation wire contract (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-protocol"></a>

Apply input MUST be one JSON object containing `operationId`, `action`, `actor` and `requestId`. Actor shape MUST follow [RFC-0011](../rfc/RFC-0011.md). Operation and request identities MUST be unique within the canonical repository. IDs MUST be bounded nonempty printable strings. Unknown operation fields MUST be rejected. Reusing an operation identity with a changed action, actor, signer key identity, target, precondition or other semantic input MUST fail with `COORD_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.

`publish` MUST additionally contain `target`, `requestedOperation`, `writeTargets` and `description`. `target` MUST retain the existing collaboration shape: `repoId`, `kind`, `id`, nullable `version`, `contentDigest`, nullable `commit`. Requested operation MUST be `review`, `draft`, `edit` or `implement`. Review MUST have empty `writeTargets`. Other operations MUST have a nonempty unique list of existing artifact IDs including the target ID. Publishing MUST capture each write artifact's exact source target. The first version MUST NOT create source artifacts. The fixed target and write inputs MUST be current when publishing, granting or transferring authority, and accepting an effective completion. An explicit target code commit MUST retain its meaning independently of coordination HEAD.

Every action after publish MUST contain `expectedState`, `expectedGeneration` and `expectedWrites`. These MUST identify the request's last state-event ID, its request generation and the full applicable map of artifact IDs to write generations. Claim MUST name the full immutable write scope. Operations on a held request MUST name all held write scopes. Cancellation of an open request and every read-only review MUST use an empty write map. Ownership-changing transitions MUST advance affected generations; a handoff offer MUST advance state-event identity without changing ownership generations.

`claim`, `accept` and `takeover` MUST include a new `holder` object containing `subjectId`, `claimId` and `sessionId`. These attempt identifiers MUST remain distinct from contributor identity. Claim MUST require an open request and free write scopes. Acceptance MUST require the offered subject and still-current offer. Takeover MUST require active ownership, an explicit takeover authorization and a nonempty `reason`.

`handoff`, `release` and `complete` MUST include the current `claimId` and `sessionId`. Handoff MUST include `toSubjectId` and `checkpoint`, with checkpoint fields `summary`, nullable `commit` and `remaining`. A new valid offer MAY replace an earlier offer using current causal preconditions. Release MUST return the request to open and invalidate the offer and claims. `cancel` MUST include a nonempty `reason` and MUST make an open or held request terminal while invalidating ownership.

`complete` MUST contain a `result` with nonempty `summary` and optional `verdict`, nullable `commit` and `references`. Verdict, when present, MUST be `approved`, `changes_requested` or `comment`; references MUST be bounded textual evidence references. For a new apply operation, checkpoint, target and result commits, when supplied, MUST be immutable object IDs reachable from the canonical remote's currently advertised branches or tags; an unpublished local commit MUST be rejected. Granting or transferring authority and accepting an effective completion MUST also validate current reachability of the fixed request code target. A pushed feature-branch commit MAY be referenced before merge to main. An effective completion MUST be terminal and release write ownership. It MUST record an outcome reference, without applying source changes or establishing a legacy standalone review approval.

`complete` MAY specify `allowObsolete: true` to append explicitly ineffective evidence. The supplied expected state, generation, holder, claim/session and input MUST match a real accepted historical attempt. This mode MUST still authorize the actor and MUST NOT change the current state, holder, result or generations. Fabricated attempts MUST be rejected. For holder-bound actions an optional `onBehalfOf` MUST follow [RFC-0012:C-POLICY](../rfc/RFC-0012.md#rfc-0012c-policy).

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0012:C-HISTORY] Signed control history and publication integrity (Normative) <a id="rfc-0012c-history"></a>

Every accepted operation MUST use an existing formatVersion 2, type `execution`, signed collaboration envelope under `gov/collaboration/<kind>/<artifactId>/<eventId>.json`. Its payload MUST contain `protocol: "govctl-coordination-v1"`, the full `operation`, `semanticDigest`, exact `parentCommit`, and `authority` with `id` and policy `revision`. The semantic digest MUST be SHA-256 over the canonical JSON object `{"operation": operation, "issuerKeyId": signature.keyId}`, using the canonical JSON conventions of [RFC-0011](../rfc/RFC-0011.md). The stored operation MUST preserve every supplied semantic input field; an implementation MUST NOT silently replace its input with different defaults. Publication-parent witness, envelope timestamp and signature MAY differ on a retry; semantic operation identity MUST NOT.

Accepted history MUST follow actual canonical main first-parent commit order, never client timestamps or filename ordering. A control record MUST first enter main in a one-parent commit containing exactly its one new control-record path, with signed `parentCommit` equal to the actual parent. Its source, policy and ownership validity MUST be determined against that predecessor. Existing accepted control records MUST NOT be modified or deleted. Invalid control history or missing policy context MUST fail closed rather than silently dropping an ownership transition. Non-coordination collaboration records MUST retain their interpretation and MUST NOT be promoted to control events.

Publication MUST use ordinary fast-forward semantics without force, local repository hook execution, arbitrary shell execution or protection bypass. Remote hooks and branch protections MUST remain effective. A lost publication race MUST trigger semantic revalidation before any retry; a rebase or merge alone MUST NOT authorize the intent. A retry MAY publish only while the same semantic preconditions remain valid. An ambiguous transport failure MUST reconcile the operation identity against newly observed canonical history before reporting success. If acceptance cannot be established, it MUST report `COORD_PUBLICATION_UNKNOWN` without granting new ownership. The first version MUST reject unsupported PR or merge-queue publication rather than claim it has validated their final update.

Historical code-reference reachability MUST be treated as the trusted issuer's assertion at publication, not as a reconstruction of past remote branch or tag references. Replay MUST retain the fixed immutable commit identity and validate the event signature, publication parent and policy applicable then. A later deletion of a referenced feature branch or tag MUST NOT erase accepted control history or ownership. New authority and effective results MUST still satisfy the current reachability requirements in [RFC-0012:C-PROTOCOL](../rfc/RFC-0012.md#rfc-0012c-protocol).

*Since: v0.1.0*
